title: Electricity 2026 — Executive summary
date_evidence: IEA warns AI data centre electricity use will triple by 2030 | Engineering and Technology Magazine — eandt.theiet.org/2026/04/22/iea-warns-ai-data-centre-electricity-use-will-triple-2030 — referring to the IEA Electricity 2026 publication released in April 2026
key_claim: Global data centre electricity demand grew 17% in 2025; AI-focused data centre demand surged ~50% and will roughly triple to about 950 TWh by 2030; tech-major capex reached USD 400 bn in 2025 with a further 75% increase expected in 2026.

title: BloombergNEF Finds Global Energy Transition Investment Reached Record $2.3 Trillion in 2025, Up 8% from 2024
key_claim: Global energy transition investment hit a record USD 2.3 trillion in 2025 (up 8% YoY); electrified transport led at USD 893 bn, renewables at USD 690 bn, grids at USD 483 bn; renewables fell 9.5%; China posted its first renewables-funding decline since 2013; energy-transition debt issuance USD 1.2 trillion (up 17%).
signals_supported: Energy-transition capital still rising but decelerating

title: New U.S. electric generating capacity expected to reach a record high in 2026
date_evidence: In-brief analysis — February 20, 2026 — New U.S. electric generating capacity expected to reach a record high in 2026
key_claim: U.S. utility-scale capacity additions in 2026 planned at a record 86 GW, of which solar 51%, battery storage 28%, wind 14%, natural gas 7%; 24 GW of battery storage vs 15 GW in 2025; Texas dominates solar (40%) and storage (53%).

title: PJM capacity prices hit record high as grid operator falls short of reliability target
key_claim: PJM's 2027-28 capacity auction cleared at the $333.44/MW-day price cap (third record auction in a row); USD 16.4 bn total cost; PJM procured 145,777 MW, 6,625 MW below the 20% reserve target; demand forecast raised by 5,250 MW almost entirely from data centres; without the Pennsylvania price cap the price would have been ~$530/MW-day.

title: Climate change presses on: Devastating wildfires and intense thunderstorms exacerbate losses for insurers (Natural disaster figures 2025)
date_evidence: Munich Re media release datestamp: 01/13/2026 (13 January 2026) — 'Climate change presses on: Devastating wildfires and intense thunderstorms exacerbate losses for insurers' — Reinsurance
key_claim: 2025 natural-disaster overall losses USD 224 bn; insured losses USD 108 bn (sixth year above USD 100 bn); weather disasters 92% of losses; non-peak perils (wildfire, severe convective storm, flood) totalled USD 166 bn / USD 98 bn insured; LA wildfires USD 53 bn / USD 40 bn insured was the costliest event; 2025 one of the warmest years on record.

title: sigma 1/2026: Natural catastrophes — wildfires, storms and floods account for record 92% of global insured losses in 2025
date_evidence: Insurance Journal — 2026/03/23 — 'Wildfires, Storms, Floods Account for Record 92% of Global Insured Losses: Swiss Re' — describing Swiss Re sigma 1/2026 release of March 23, 2026
key_claim: 2025 insured natural-catastrophe losses USD 107 bn (sixth consecutive year >USD 100 bn); secondary perils — wildfires, severe convective storms, floods — accounted for a record 92%; modelled peak-year scenario could push 2026 insured losses to ~USD 320 bn.

title: Queued Up: 2025 Edition — Characteristics of Power Plants Seeking Transmission Interconnection As of the End of 2024
date_evidence: PDF filename and titlepage: queued_up_2025_edition_12.15.2025.pdf — Berkeley Lab Energy Markets & Planning publication, December 2025
key_claim: U.S. interconnection queue at end-2024 holds ~11,600 projects, 2,600 GW (1,570 GW generation + 1,030 GW storage), more than double installed U.S. capacity (1,279 GW); 95% of capacity is solar/storage/wind; median request-to-COD duration has doubled from <2 years (2000-2007 cohort) to >4 years (2018-2024 cohort).

title: Near-700 GW Surge in 2025 Proves Renewable Energy Resilience — Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026
date_evidence: IRENA Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026 — irena.org/Publications/2026/Mar/Renewable-capacity-statistics-2026 — 'Renewable capacity highlights — 31 March 2026'
key_claim: Global renewable capacity reached 5,149 GW after a record 692 GW addition in 2025 (+15.5% YoY); solar 511 GW (75% of additions), wind 159 GW; renewables 85.6% of all capacity additions; Asia 74.2% of new renewable capacity (513 GW).

title: Energy Storage Enters the 100-Gigawatt Era: Three Things to Know
date_evidence: ess-news.com/2026/05/11/bloombergnef-confirms-energy-storage-has-reached-the-100-gw-era — BNEF confirms 2025 annual additions of 112 GW / 307 GWh, up 48% YoY
key_claim: Annual energy-storage additions (excluding pumped hydro) reached 112 GW / 307 GWh in 2025 — up 48% YoY — crossing 100 GW for the first time; BNEF projects 158 GW / 459 GWh in 2026 (+41%); storage hit 100 GW in 4 years vs 8 for solar and 15 for wind.

title: NRC Issues First Commercial Reactor Construction Approval in 10 Years For TerraPower in Wyoming
date_evidence: No: 26-028 March 4, 2026 — CONTACT: Scott Burnell — NRC Issues First Commercial Reactor Construction Approval in 10 Years For TerraPower in Wyoming
key_claim: NRC authorised staff on 4 March 2026 to issue TerraPower's US SFR Owner a construction permit for the 345-MWe Natrium plant at Kemmerer, Wyoming — the first commercial reactor construction approval in nearly a decade and first non-light-water-reactor approval in over 40 years; technical review took under 18 months.
signals_supported: Firm clean capacity for data centres
verbatim_quote: first commercial reactor the NRC has approved for construction in nearly a decade and the first approval for a non-light water reactor in more than 40 years

title: European Climate Resilience and Risk Management — Integrated Framework
date_evidence: European Commission programme page describing the forthcoming Integrated Framework for European Climate Resilience and Risk Management to be adopted H2 2026 — accessed 28/05/2026
key_claim: European Commission is developing an Integrated Framework for European Climate Resilience and Risk Management to be adopted H2 2026; consultation called for resilience-by-design, harmonised climate risk assessments, nature-based solutions and stable long-term adaptation finance; economic damages to infrastructure already average ~EUR 45 bn/year.

title: The Critical Entities Resilience Directive: Compliance Readiness Before and After July 2026
date_evidence: International SOS / Deloitte commentary on CER Directive compliance dated February 2026 (2026-02-15) — referencing 17 July 2026 designation deadline; Member-State strategy deadline was 17 January 2026; ten-month compliance clock starts on designation, latest compliance May 2027
key_claim: EU Critical Entities Resilience Directive: Member-State strategy deadline 17 January 2026 already passed; critical-entity designation deadline 17 July 2026; designated entities have 10 months to comply, with latest compliance date May 2027 across 11 sectors including energy, transport, water and digital infrastructure.

title: Emissions Gap Report 2025: Off Target — Continued Collective Inaction Puts Global Temperature Goal at Risk
date_evidence: UNEP — published 4 November 2025 — Emissions Gap Report 2025 'Off Target'; press release: 'New climate pledges only slightly lower dangerous global warming projections'
key_claim: Full implementation of new NDCs puts global warming at 2.3-2.5°C (vs 2.6-2.8°C in last year's report); current policies yield up to 2.8°C; reductions of 35% (2°C path) and 55% (1.5°C path) below 2019 levels required by 2035; temporary 1.5°C overshoot now considered inevitable from the early 2030s.

title: Copernicus: 2025 was the third hottest year on record
date_evidence: Copernicus Climate Bulletin — 'Copernicus: 2025 was the third hottest year on record' — January 2026 global temperature report stating 2023-2025 three-year average exceeded 1.5°C above pre-industrial for the first time
key_claim: Global average temperature in 2025 was 14.97°C, 0.59°C above the 1991-2020 average and 0.13°C below 2024 (the warmest year); 2023-2025 was the first three-year period to average more than 1.5°C above pre-industrial; January 2025 was the warmest January on record.

title: Even Low-Risk Homes Are Caught Up in California's Climate Insurance Crisis
date_evidence: Insurance Journal — insurancejournal.com/news/west/2026/03/16/862079.htm — 'Even Low-Risk Homes Are Caught Up in California's Climate Insurance Crisis' — March 16, 2026
key_claim: California FAIR Plan enrolment surged 43% between September 2024 and December 2025 as insurers retreated post-LA wildfires; 14% of current FAIR policies are in low-fire-risk urban zones; insurer withdrawal now extends beyond high-risk areas; the LA wildfires generated USD 40 bn in insured losses.

title: Facing a Hostile Administration, U.S. Offshore Wind Is in Retreat
date_evidence: Yale E360 — 'Facing a Hostile Administration, U.S. Offshore Wind Is in Retreat' — April 2026 feature describing Atlantic Shores cancellation, Empire Wind stop-work order in April followed by May resumption after governor-administration negotiation
key_claim: US offshore wind sector in retreat in 2026: Atlantic Shores 1.5 GW project formally cancelled and EPA revoked its air-quality permit in March; Empire Wind hit by a stop-work order in April but allowed to resume in May after gubernatorial negotiation; Department of Interior briefly paused all five large in-construction projects on national-security grounds.

title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act to Scale Back Clean Energy Tax Credits Under Inflation Reduction Act
date_evidence: Holland & Knight client alert describing OBBBA signed by President Trump on 4 July 2025; accelerated IRA phase-out — almost all residential credits gone by end-2025; wind and solar facilities beginning construction after 4 July 2026 must be placed in service by 31 December 2027 to qualify
key_claim: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed 4 July 2025) accelerates IRA phase-out: residential credits ended by end-2025; Section 45Y and 48E (clean electricity production and investment credits) wound down with a 4 July 2026 construction-start trigger requiring service by 31 December 2027; EV charger credit ends 30 June 2026; tighter Foreign-Entity-of-Concern rules narrow eligible supply chains.
